correctness.rationale: For two scalar positive-curvature quadratics and complete averaging W=(11^T)/2, the local gradient secant equals h_i whenever defined; initialized adaptive alpha_i=q/h_i remains constant under the specified local-gradient step rule. The tracking invariant sum y_i=sum grad_i and primal consensus after the first averaging step give error recurrence e_(k+1)=(1-q)e_k-q*xi*e_(k-1), xi=(h1-h2)^2/(4*h1*h2). Its characteristic polynomial r²+(q-1)r+qxi is strictly Schur stable iff qxi<1 and q(1-xi)<2; the active bound changes at xi=1/3: qcrit=2/(1-xi) below and 1/xi above. The full 4x4 state has factors r(r-1) times this quadratic; r=1 is excluded on the legitimate gradient-tracking invariant subspace. Independently reconstructed symbolic 4x4 update characteristic polynomial and tested eight rational stable/unstable parameter cases spanning both branches; exactly reproduced source algebra, not relying on standalone verifier status. Unit roots on the boundary are not asymptotically stable.

value.rationale: The two-agent complete-averaging quadratic specialization is the minimal nontrivial model of curvature heterogeneity for adaptive gradient tracking. Its exact stability frontier and flip-versus-unit-circle transition show how reciprocal-curvature steps can fail despite scalar local smoothness control, sharpening conservative general network tuning without pretending to be a general theorem.
